title: Overview: the big ideas
summary: The chapter's key concepts and how its sections fit together.

blocks.md: Welcome to **Robust AI** (Vol II). This overview gives you the chapter's big ideas before the section-by-section lessons. Read the claims once, flip the flashcards, then take the warm-up quiz: it is fine to miss questions here, the lessons that follow fill the gaps.

A model service can maintain stable latency and uptime while its predictions become unreliable. Changes in operating conditions, manipulated inputs, or corrupted computation may leave ordinary health signals untouched, allowing errors to affect decisions long before business metrics expose them. Conventional software can also fail silently; machine learning adds statistical failures that a successful request cannot reveal. At fleet scale, replicating a model across healthy machines does not remove a weakness shared by every copy.

nodes.label: A Unified Framework for Robust AI

rows: Drift, adversarial inputs, poisoning, and silent faults can keep every service-health signal green while predictions become invalid, and replication does not remove a weakness every copy shares, so robustness is claimed only per stated failure class.

Covariate shift changes P(x), label shift changes P(y), and concept drift changes P(y|x), so input monitors can be silent under pure concept drift and the type of shift selects the remedy (reweighting, recalibration, or adaptation on fresh labels).

A drift alert opens an investigation rather than a retrain: detection, correlation with outcome performance, and action are separate levels, and a model update needs labels that confirm the shift and a root cause the update addresses.

Population monitors cannot say whether one request lies inside demonstrated competence, so serving trades coverage against selective risk along a threshold, and conformal prediction adds a coverage guarantee that holds only under exchangeability.
**Adversarial robustness for a named threat model**

Attacker access defines the evaluation a defense must survive (for a physical attack, the full sensor loop rather than saved images), and robustness is bought empirically in training compute (adversarial training multiplies passes per batch) or certifiably in serving samples.

Because poisoned records can preserve clean aggregate accuracy, defense runs as ordered layers along the data path (ingress controls, anomaly detection and sanitization, robust training, post-training checks), each with a named blind spot, made reversible by lineage.
A hallucination rate is meaningful only against a stated evidence source, prompt set, and decoding settings, and entropy and self-consistency are priced routing signals, not factuality scores.

A preprocessing bug moves feature statistics like covariate shift and a numerical overflow flips decisions like an adversarial example, so operators read system evidence (timing against releases, fixed-input replay, cross-layer correlation) before choosing a defense.
Adversarial examples crafted on a surrogate often transfer to the deployed model, which makes black-box attacks practical without gradient access.
